description: telemetry.v1 §2.5, §2.6: a resolved resource, as declarations.json writes it, and one sample -> its conformance, and the member's kind and unit as the sample gives them. sample is {"undecodable": true} (bytes the core could not decode), or {value, attachment?}: the decoded data item and the decoded attachment, absent when the sample has none; or, since 0.2, the bytes as they came: json_text, the payload's bytes as UTF-8 text, read as strict JSON (UTF-8, RFC 8259, nothing after the value but whitespace, no duplicate member at any depth, no lone surrogate escape, every number finite: anything else is undecodable), or cbor_hex, the payload's bytes in hex, read as CBOR (an integer is major type 0 or 1, or a bignum, tag 2 or 3 around a byte string of any length, the integer it denotes; every other tag, and a tag 2 or 3 around anything else, its content; map keys text, none twice; undefined is null: anything else is undecodable); and attachment_text, the attachment's bytes as UTF-8 text, read as JSON, an attachment that does not decode being an epoch present and not a string. A data item is written as JSON, read by its text: a number with no fraction and no exponent is an integer, read exactly; any other number is the IEEE double it denotes. Three objects of one member stand for what this file's JSON cannot hold: {"$int": "<decimal>"} an integer outside -2^63 to 2^64-1, {"$float": "NaN" | "Infinity" | "-Infinity"} a float that is not finite (CBOR carries them), {"$bytes": "<base64>"} a byte string (a raw payload's bytes). An integer as JSON Schema's integer reads one is an integer, or an integral finite float, the integer it equals; an integer's text is read exactly, however long. A member written null is present, and null is no string and no object. expect.conformance is conforms, does_not (reasons, every one that applies, in this order, each check made alone and a check that needs a value an earlier one found wrong skipped: not_a_point, epoch_invalid, unit_invalid, tag_disagrees, unit_disagrees, wrong_type, out_of_range, not_finite, bounds_invalid, bounds_differ, counts_length, count_sum, as v1.md §2.6 defines them), unobservable (declaration_invalid, or undecodable) or not_asked (not_this_profiles, or ignored); reasons is [] when it conforms. A Point is an object with timestamp an integer from -2^63 to 2^63-1, value an object with type one of the six kinds and a member value, labels, if present, an object of strings, and unit, if present, a string; other members are tolerated, and a Point that is not one is checked no further. An in-band epoch (a Point's epoch, or, for a bare counter or histogram whose declaration's epoch is attachment, the attachment) is a string of 1 to 64 Unicode code points. A value's kind is the Point's tag, or the declared kind for a bare value. expect.kind and expect.unit are the member's kind and unit as this sample gives them, and kind_from and unit_from where each came from (declared, or point), null when none: the declared kind and unit always, unless the declaration is invalid or not asked; the Point's tag and its unit only when the sample conforms. A null unit is unknown, never dimensionless.
